title: Unit Economics KPI Pack (FY2026) — Draft (Internal)
content:
Redwood Inference — FY2026 Unit Economics KPI Pack (DRAFT)
Owner: Laura Bennett (CFO)
FP&A owner: Rishi Malhotra
Last updated: 2026-02-16
Audience: ELT + VP Eng/Product + Finance + SRE
Source of truth: Internal Unit Economics Dashboard (v1) + Finance rate card + reconciliation view

NOTES / STATUS
- This is a draft outline + speaker notes for the FY2026 exec KPI deck. It assumes the Unit Economics Dashboard v1 is live and finance-aligned.
- Numbers below are placeholders until Finance signoff is complete (see “Signoff / Open Items” slide).
- KPI focus is blended cost per output token (primary) + drivers (secondary) + reliability/quality guardrails.

============================================================
SLIDE 1 — TITLE
Title: FY2026 Unit Economics (Inference) — KPI Pack
Subtitle: Blended $/1M Output Tokens + Drivers + Guardrails
Footer: Internal — Finance/Eng shared metric

Speaker notes:
- This pack is designed for QBR cadence and quarterly board/executive reporting.
- Metric definitions are aligned to Finance methodology v1; dashboard provides drilldowns by model / region / customer tier.

============================================================
SLIDE 2 — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (1 slide)
Bullets (fill in at QBR time):
- Blended cost improved/worsened by ___% QoQ driven by: (1) ___, (2) ___, (3) ___.
- Top outliers this quarter: Model ___ in region ___ (tier ___) due to ___.
- Reliability/quality guardrails: No/Yes incidents impacting cost reporting; dashboard data confidence is ___.
- Actions in flight next quarter: streaming metering parity, batching utilization improvements, quant profile rollout, region normalization hardening.

Speaker notes:
- Keep this to 60 seconds. Use “what changed / why / what we’re doing.”

============================================================
SLIDE 3 — KPI DEFINITIONS (FINANCE-ALIGNED)
Header: Primary KPI
Definition:
- Blended $/1M output tokens = (Allocated inference serving costs) / (Total metered output tokens) * 1,000,000
- Reported by: day, week, month (finance view = month-end aligned)

Inclusions (high level):
- GPU compute (hosted + dedicated + private fleets where applicable)
- Allocated shared overhead (control plane, routing/gateway where scoped) — per ADR-034
- Idle capacity treatment — per ADR-034 and rate card notes

Exclusions (high level):
- Non-inference R&D spend
- Support costs (unless explicitly allocated in methodology revision)

Data sources:
- Token metering pipeline (output_tokens)
- GPU cost rate card (versioned; 2025Q4 baseline; FY2026 cadence TBD)
- Reconciliation report vs billing totals (internal)

Speaker notes:
- Emphasize “blended” = allocation-based, not marginal.
- Reinforce that this reconciles to finance inputs and has an audit trail (rate card version + methodology version).

============================================================
SLIDE 4 — FY2026 KPI TARGETS (PROPOSED) — COMPANY LEVEL
Table (placeholders; finalize after signoff)
KPI: Blended $/1M Output Tokens (All tiers, all regions, weighted by output tokens)
- FY2025 exit (baseline): $___ per 1M output tokens
- FY2026 target range:
  - H1: $___ – $___
  - H2: $___ – $___
- Stretch target (if optimization roadmap lands): $___ by end of FY2026

Notes:
- Target is a range to reflect mix shifts (model mix, region mix, tier mix).
- A separate “Finance view” and “Live view” may differ slightly due to freshness windows; KPI reporting uses Finance view.

Speaker notes:
- Call out the operational levers that make the target realistic: caching, batching, quantization, kernel improvements, fleet purchasing strategy.

============================================================
SLIDE 5 — KPI TARGETS BY CUSTOMER TIER (PROPOSED)
Header: Targets are directional; use for diagnosing mix shifts, not performance rating

Tiers:
- Self-serve (Hosted API)
- Dedicated
- Private
- Enterprise (contractual; may overlap with Dedicated/Private in ops)

Table (placeholder):
Tier | FY2025 exit $/1M | FY2026 target range | Key assumptions
Self-serve | $___ | $___–$___ | higher batching benefits; higher variance
Dedicated | $___ | $___–$___ | idle allocation sensitivity; contract mix
Private | $___ | $___–$___ | customer-managed constraints; region limits
Enterprise | $___ | $___–$___ | mix-driven; negotiated pricing vs cost

Commentary placeholders:
- Mix shift explanation: If blended total moves but per-tier stable, highlight token volume shift.
- Contract-specific caveat: Dedicated/Private may have bespoke fleet pricing not fully reflected until rate card update.

Speaker notes:
- Tier targets should not be used as “team OKRs” without context; they’re diagnostic bands.

============================================================
SLIDE 6 — TOP DRIVERS OF UNIT COST (WHAT WE EXPECT TO MOVE THE KPI)
Driver list (to be supported by dashboard drilldowns):
1) Model mix (architecture + size)
2) Quantization profile adoption (e.g., fp16 vs int8/int4) [guardrails apply]
3) Region mix (cloud region vs internal colo; different $/GPU-hour)
4) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache)
5) Batching efficiency (avg batch size, continuous batching utilization)
6) Output length / completion length distribution
7) Streaming vs non-streaming path differences (metering parity + overhead)
8) Prefill/decode ratio shifts (long-context workloads)

Speaker notes:
- Use this slide to align on “what to look at first” when KPI changes.

============================================================
SLIDE 7 — DASHBOARD SNAPSHOT (PLACEHOLDER)
Insert screenshot (TBD):
- Time series: blended $/1M output tokens (last 90 days)
- Top-N: models by total tokens + unit cost
- Filters: time range, model, region, tier, quant profile

Callouts:
- “Confidence” indicator is required for exec view (coverage & completeness).
- Direct links to reconciliation view and data quality status.

Speaker notes:
- If presenting live, show “Finance view” default.
- Show how to drill into a spike: model -> region -> tier -> drivers.

============================================================
SLIDE 8 — MODEL-LEVEL OUTLIERS (TOP-N)
Template table:
Rank | Model (version) | Quant profile | $/1M output tokens | WoW change | Token share | Notes / Hypothesis
1 | ___ | ___ | $___ | ___% | ___% | ___
2 | ___ | ___ | $___ | ___% | ___% | ___
3 | ___ | ___ | $___ | ___% | ___% | ___

Commentary placeholders:
- Are we seeing performance regressions vs planned changes?
- Any version rollouts / kernel changes / routing changes?

Speaker notes:
- Keep to 3–5 items. Tie to specific engineering actions.

============================================================
SLIDE 9 — REGION-LEVEL OUTLIERS
Template:
- Heatmap or table by region (canonical normalized regions)
Region | $/1M output tokens | Token volume | GPU $/hr index | Notes
us-east | $___ | ___ | ___ | ___
eu-west | $___ | ___ | ___ | ___
ap-sg | $___ | ___ | ___ | ___

Commentary placeholders:
- Identify whether the delta is cost-rate-driven (rate card) vs utilization-driven (batching/caching) vs demand pattern.
- Flag any region mapping issues (unknown/null) impacting coverage.

Speaker notes:
- If a region spikes, ensure we mention whether it’s “real” or a data issue (confidence indicator).

============================================================
SLIDE 10 — QUANTIZATION: COST VS QUALITY GUARDRAILS
Template narrative:
- Quant profiles in use (allowed values): ___
- Adoption trend: % tokens served under each profile (last 30/90 days)
- Observed cost impact: $/1M delta vs baseline profile (controlled where possible)
- Quality guardrails status:
  - Eval set pass rate: ___
  - Customer incident rate related to quality: ___
  - Rollback/fallback events: ___

Speaker notes:
- Make explicit: cost wins must be paired with eval confidence and rollback policy.

============================================================
SLIDE 11 — CACHE & BATCHING (OPERATIONAL DRIVERS)
Template charts (TBD):
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) vs unit cost correlation
- Batching utilization vs unit cost correlation

Talking points placeholders:
- Cache: Changes due to routing / prompt prefix stability / cache keying changes.
- Batching: Changes due to traffic shape, latency SLO constraints, or runtime upgrades.

Speaker notes:
- These are the levers Optimize will operationalize; Finance wants them as “explainability,” not as KPIs.

============================================================
SLIDE 12 — METERING & DATA QUALITY (TRUST)
Minimum required checks for exec reporting (SLO-backed):
- Freshness: hourly pipeline completeness >= ___% within ___ minutes
- Dimension coverage:
  - Unknown/NULL region <= ___%
  - Unknown tier <= ___%
  - Unknown model/version <= ___%
  - Unknown quant profile <= ___%
- Reconciliation vs billing (monthly): within ___% (or explain known deltas)

Incident + oncall:
- Oncall rotation: Eng Telemetry/Analytics + SRE (primary); Finance escalation path defined
- Runbook link: (TBD) oncall-guide-unit-economics-dashboard

Speaker notes:
- If any threshold is breached, KPI slide should show “Data confidence: degraded” and avoid over-interpreting week-over-week changes.

============================================================
SLIDE 13 — RECONCILIATION VIEW (FINANCE CHECK)
Template:
- Dashboard totals vs Billing totals (tokens, $) for month-end
- Known differences list (pre-approved):
  1) Timing windows (usage cutoffs)
  2) Credits/promos treatment (if excluded from cost)
  3) Dedicated contract accounting vs platform metering scope

Placeholder table:
Month | Dashboard tokens | Billing tokens | Delta | Dashboard allocated cost | Billing revenue (context only) | Notes
___ | ___ | ___ | ___ | ___ | ___ | ___

Speaker notes:
- Reinforce that this KPI is a cost metric, not revenue. Billing reconciliation is for token metering parity and scope alignment.

============================================================
SLIDE 14 — FY2026 ROADMAP (WHAT IMPROVES THE KPI)
Buckets:
1) Runtime efficiency: kernels, continuous batching, KV cache management
2) Optimize automation: recommended configs, regressions detection
3) Fleet economics: reserved capacity mix, region procurement strategy, idle reduction
4) Data maturity: better attribution, clearer segmentation, stable rate card versioning

Template list (tie to owners):
- Batch utilization instrumentation + adoption (Owner: Dylan / Runtime)
- Output token metering parity across streaming/tool calls (Owner: Nadia / Telemetry)
- Rate card versioning + quarterly update process (Owner: Rishi / FP&A)
- Dashboard finance view locked at month-end (Owner: Marissa / Console)

Speaker notes:
- Tie each item to expected $/1M impact range when possible (even if broad).

============================================================
SLIDE 15 — RISKS / CAVEATS
Risk list (draft):
- Mix shift volatility: model/region/tier mix can swamp efficiency improvements.
- Allocation debates: idle capacity + shared overhead assumptions can change reported blended cost.
- Data completeness: missing dimensions or token undercount (esp streaming) can bias $/1M.
- Behavioral risk: teams optimize for KPI at expense of latency/quality.

Mitigations:
- Publish methodology + versioning; require signoff for changes.
- Confidence indicator & guardrails (latency/quality) shown alongside cost KPI.
- Separate “live ops view” vs “finance reporting view.”

Speaker notes:
- Name the caveats proactively so the deck is credible.

============================================================
SLIDE 16 — DECISIONS NEEDED / SIGNOFF CHECKLIST
Finance signoff checklist (must be true before FY2026 KPI is “official”):
- Methodology v1 approved (ADR-034 aligned) — Owner: Laura/Rishi — Status: ___
- Rate card provenance + cadence documented; versioned in reporting — Owner: Rishi — Status: ___
- Reconciliation report within threshold for last 2 month-ends — Owner: Logan/Mei + FP&A — Status: ___
- Tier mapping source-of-truth documented + tested — Owner: Logan + Platform — Status: ___
- Region normalization coverage >= threshold — Owner: Mei — Status: ___
- Exec view uses “Finance view” with month-end close behavior — Owner: Marissa — Status: ___

Speaker notes:
- This slide should be updated weekly during rollout and removed after signoff.

============================================================
APPENDIX A — GLOSSARY (OPTIONAL)
- Output tokens: tokens generated by the model (excluding input tokens)
- Blended cost: allocated cost divided by metered tokens; includes overhead/idle per methodology
- Quantization profile: serving precision/config that affects throughput/cost/quality
- Cache hit rate: fraction of requests/tokens benefiting from prefix/KV cache reuse
- Batching efficiency: utilization of continuous batching; impacts GPU occupancy

============================================================
APPENDIX B — PLACEHOLDER TARGET RATIONALE (FOR INTERNAL REVIEW)
(Working notes; not for exec consumption)
- Target range should be set using:
  - FY2025 exit run-rate
  - Expected model mix (new models onboarded, version changes)
  - Expected efficiency gains (batching/caching/quant)
  - Fleet purchasing plan (reserved vs on-demand)
- Proposed approach:
  1) Lock FY2025 baseline month (e.g., Sep/Oct) after reconciliation
  2) Produce sensitivity bands: mix-only vs efficiency-only vs combined
  3) Publish H1/H2 bands; refresh mid-year if rate card changes materially

END
